evidence_extracts.locator: S1 Abstract/sections 3,6; S2 sections 3–5/Appendix C; S3 Abstract/Methods/contributions
evidence_extracts.observed_claim: AI Scientist v1 executed ML experiments and generated manuscripts from human-provided topic templates in diffusion, language modelling and learning dynamics; its conference-threshold assessment used an automated reviewer. V2 removed topic-code templates, added experiment management/tree search and vision feedback, and submitted three unedited generated manuscripts to an ICLR workshop; one achieved mean review score 6.33. The 2026 journal article describes the result as passing first-round workshop review, with a 70% workshop acceptance rate.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Computational research and manuscript production were executed; extending the approach to physics or biology in v1 was a suggested application, not its demonstration.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Humans chose the domain/setup and selected submissions; the later article explicitly credits human reading, validation and implementation checks. External workshop review differs from the internal automated reviewer.
evidence_extracts.limitations: Manuscripts were withdrawn by advance protocol. Do not describe the generated workshop manuscript as a published Nature scientific discovery. V2's own team reports possible dataset overlap, unclear method descriptions and caption errors; workshop evidence is a small selected sample.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Gentle prior-work citation for broader automation ambitions, explicitly separated from this guide's human-directed physics workflow.

evidence_extracts.observed_claim: An independent execution study of the original AI Scientist found five of twelve proposed experiments failed with code errors; other outputs included misleading goal/metric relationships and invented numerical results in manuscripts. It documents setup effort as well as complete manuscript generation.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Third-party system execution, not an opinion-only critique.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Evaluation performed by researchers outside the originating team; setup and execution carried out by their third author, a Python-proficient bachelor student.
evidence_extracts.limitations: One domain (green recommender systems), MovieLens-100k, one template and fixed seed ideas. This is counterevidence about that original configuration; it cannot establish failure rates for v2, the 2026 system, other domains or current frontier models.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Supports checking methods, code and numerical claims separately from fluency; cite with its narrow denominator.

evidence_extracts.locator: Sections 3.3.1 and 4.2.2, particularly external evaluation and comparison with autonomous mode
evidence_extracts.observed_claim: Agent Laboratory takes a human research idea through literature review, experimentation and report/code production, with autonomous and co-pilot modes. External evaluators scored co-pilot papers 0.58 points higher overall than autonomous papers; gains were larger in quality and soundness than contribution or significance.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Research pipeline and human feedback sessions were executed; the separate MLE-Bench evaluation concerns its code solver, not independent validity of whole papers.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Humans supply ideas and optional phase feedback; external paper reviewers assess outcomes. Model self-review and researcher self-assessment are additional, distinct measurements.
evidence_extracts.limitations: Small research-study ratings and selected topics do not establish universal human-feedback causality or equal performance across scientific domains. Overall co-pilot external score was 4.38/10, so improvement should not be paraphrased as conference-quality research.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Direct precedent for useful human guidance without asserting that all research must be fully autonomous.

evidence_extracts.observed_claim: AgentRxiv lets agent laboratories upload/retrieve reports and build on prior runs. Authors report 13.7% relative improvement over baseline MATH-500 accuracy with multiple sharing labs; this tests reasoning/prompting research, not general science.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Collaborative computational runs executed. Humans provided initial direction and detailed instructions.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Authors manually verified each reported program output and corresponding code before reporting accuracy.
evidence_extracts.limitations: Authors observed code repair removing core functionality or printing realistic-looking results without the intended computation, and manuscript numbers mismatching experiments. Novelty remained uncertain. A shared report server supports communication but does not supply independent verification; collaborators can propagate the same error.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Useful author-reported failure mechanisms behind a requirement to inspect executable evidence; acknowledge the measured collaboration gain.

evidence_extracts.locator: S7 Key contributions/System analysis/expert workflow/Code availability; S8 version history
evidence_extracts.observed_claim: Co-Scientist generates, debates, ranks and evolves hypotheses and experimental proposals under scientist objectives. The 2026 article reports wet-laboratory validation in drug repurposing, liver fibrosis targets and antimicrobial resistance. It evaluates generated hypotheses on 15 expert-curated goals using its own Elo metric, alongside limited expert assessment.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Hypothesis generation plus subsequent laboratory validation occurred; the system's autonomous output is a proposal, not autonomous laboratory operation.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Experts define goals, review and select proposals and conduct experiments. AML setup took under one expert hour and final selection about three hours, excluding laboratory work.
evidence_extracts.limitations: Elo is an internal ranking measure; it is not empirical truth or general human-scientist equivalence. Full source is unavailable, though prompts/pseudocode are provided. Laboratory validation of selected examples does not validate every generated hypothesis.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Cite as a complementary collaborative workflow with explicit external experimental grounding; use the 2026 title/version rather than treating the 2025 announcement as the endpoint.

evidence_extracts.observed_claim: Kosmos iterates literature search and data analysis from a scientist-supplied objective and dataset, linking report claims to notebooks or literature. Experts checked 102 statements from three representative reports without receiving original code/citations: 79.4% overall supported, including 85.5% data-analysis, 82.1% literature and 57.9% synthesis statements.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Computational discovery runs and expert validation executed; report includes seven selected scientific case studies.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Scientists prepare inputs and evaluate significance; expert checks use their own analysis/search.
evidence_extracts.limitations: Statement accuracy is not whole-discovery reproducibility. Six-month equivalence is collaborator-estimated time, not a matched prospective productivity experiment. Authors report overstatement, expert-intensive checking, sensitivity to objectives and stochastic disagreement across runs.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Especially relevant distinction between traceable calculation and valid scientific interpretation; provenance improves auditability without establishing correctness.

evidence_extracts.observed_claim: AlphaEvolve evolves code against user-supplied automatic evaluators. Demonstrated outputs include mathematical constructions and improvements to Google infrastructure algorithms. It reports a 48-scalar-multiplication method for 4×4 complex matrices, with exact constructions exposed in an associated notebook.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: Code search, evaluation and selected engineering deployment occurred; scientific targets are machine-gradeable computational tasks.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Humans define initial programs, evolvable blocks and evaluation functions. Exact mathematical validity, numerical scores and deployed performance are different evidence types.
evidence_extracts.limitations: The paper explicitly excludes tasks requiring manual experimentation. A strong evaluator constrains the domain and encodes human choices; success does not establish autonomous scientific inference where the objective itself is contested.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Supports the value of executable validation while keeping algorithm optimization distinct from physics conclusions.

evidence_extracts.observed_claim: AstraZeneca describes a deployed biomedical assistant, reporting 15,000 internal users within a year. Its deep-research mode executes a bounded DAG of retrieval questions; outputs link evidence for human examination. The technical note explicitly distinguishes this from open-ended autonomous research.
evidence_extracts.actual_execution: First-party report of enterprise deployment and user feedback; no access to private enterprise data or system was used here.
evidence_extracts.human_role_and_independence: Scientists ask questions, can override research plans and inspect sources. Evaluations include internal QA regression sets, real-user feedback and LLM-assisted interaction analytics.
evidence_extracts.limitations: Adoption is not scientific-outcome validation. Authors report that useful product improvements did not improve the narrow BioASQ metric; citation-grounded web answers can still have only tangential support. No independent impact study is established.
evidence_extracts.whitepaper_use: Useful current example of a complementary bounded assistance workflow and a warning against equating benchmark gains with scientific usefulness.

method_candidates.observed: Inputs: report statements; transformation: label literature, analysis or synthesis and ask experts to independently check them without original supporting artifacts; output: support rates by claim type.
method_candidates.hypothesized_transfer: Sample physics guide claims by calculation versus interpretation, and commission separately scoped checks.
method_candidates.constraints: Independent reviewers need sufficient domain expertise; a small sampled audit cannot certify an entire paper.
method_candidates.cheapest_validation: On one existing public case, check three calculations and three interpretive claims; record disagreement and time. Proposed only; not performed.

method_candidates.observed: Inputs: claimed benchmark scores, actual program and outputs; transformation: author team manually verifies code and output correspondence; output: checked reported accuracies despite repair/hallucination failures.
method_candidates.hypothesized_transfer: Before a physics result enters prose, confirm the intended calculation remains implemented and its run record supports the number.
method_candidates.constraints: Logs alone can be fabricated; author inspection is not independent replication.
method_candidates.cheapest_validation: Audit one existing public result from claim through code path to stored numerical artifact, without launching new science. Proposed only.

method_candidates.observed: Inputs: human evaluation code and generated candidate; transformation: escalating test cascade rejects faulty or unpromising candidates early; output: scored executable programs.
method_candidates.hypothesized_transfer: Use inexpensive invariants before expensive physics validation, preserving a separately justified scientific acceptance rule.
method_candidates.constraints: Automatic scores only cover encoded properties; test leakage and objective mismatch need separate controls.
method_candidates.cheapest_validation: On one existing public example, compare a fast invariant's outcome with its established full validation record. Proposed only.

gaps: No cross-system matched comparison on the guide's physics/reproducibility tasks; neither superiority nor general frontier-model-versus-human parity is supported.

Primary papers demonstrate different units: entire ML manuscripts, hypothesis proposals, prompt benchmarks, dataset analysis and machine-gradeable algorithms. A single autonomy score would erase decisive differences.

This focused search is not exhaustive through the cutoff: Robin, Virtual Lab, Paper2Agent and newer benchmark systems deserve an appendix follow-up if space warrants. Their omission does not imply absence of evidence.

Historical Agent Laboratory/AgentRxiv versions are intentionally pinned; later revisions were not compared. Nature supplemental files and Co-Scientist's inaccessible arXiv v2 HTML were not fully inspected.
For public prose, prioritize a few contextual citations; retain detailed failure mechanisms and denominators in an appendix rather than turning this physics practice guide into a CS system survey.

Public aiXiv reference lists were inspected as discovery seeds; AstraZeneca original source was followed. Systems lane does not use our postings as independent validation or reproduce their operational claims.

contradictions.resolution: AI Scientist promotional/abstract language can suggest an accepted publication; the 2026 article says first-round review, and protocol withdrew generated submissions. Preserve the narrower procedural observation.

AgentRxiv's reported accuracy includes manual code/output verification; Co-Scientist includes expert selection and laboratory work; Kosmos includes expert validation. Attribute automation to the stages actually delegated.

Kosmos distinguishes data-analysis support from lower synthesis accuracy. Do not turn its aggregate statement-support fraction or estimated time into a general discovery-validity or speedup guarantee.

contradictions.issue: Old failure rates applied to newer systems
contradictions.resolution: Independent v1 counterevidence has a narrow domain/sample. Include alongside later systems without asserting the same rate persists.

confidence_detail.overall: high for the bounded source descriptions; moderate for transfer to physics practice
confidence_detail.basis: Versioned primary papers, primary publisher metadata and author-reported limitations checked. No independent reruns by this worker; original team claims remain attributed.
confidence_detail.positioning: These are relevant neighboring workflows, not direct competitors evaluated on the whitepaper's physics tasks. Avoid a general frontier-model-versus-human ranking.
